content.title: Is Twitter Down? X users suffer global outage
content.text: Users of the social media service X reported issues on Thursday morning, according to an outage tracker.Downdetector reported a sharp rise in users reporting problems at around 3 a.m. ET. The cause of the apparent outage was not immediately clear.Issues were widespread, with users in the United States, India, South America and parts of Europe among those reporting problems.In the United States, problems seemed to peak at around 3.20 a.m. with more than 25,000 complaints, before appearing to drop off again by around 3.30 a.m.Heat maps during the incident showed problems being reported in Los Angeles, Miami, Chicago, New York, Atlanta and Washington, D.C.One Downdetector user said: "Anyone having trouble posting? Mine keep failing," another added: "I can't view any tweets."Newsweek reached out to X in an email sent outside of regular working hours for comment.Stock image of a smartphone showing the icon for X. | Cheng Xin/Getty ImagesX is owned by billionaire Elon Musk, who acquired the company for around $44 billion, then Twitter, in 2022 and later rebranded it. The social media site is yet to provide an explanation for Thursday's reported issues on any of its official channels.It is not the first time that users have reported problems in recent months. Similar incidents have temporarily disabled core features such as accessing timelines, logging in and loading posts.X was one of a number of major digital platforms to suffer problems due to an outage at Cloudflare, a cybersecurity and web technology firm based in San Francisco last year. Other websites to report problems were ChatGPT and Uber.That followed issues at Microsoft's Azure cloud portal that left users unable to access Office 365, Minecraft and other services; and another at Amazon in October took down a broad range of online services, including social media, gaming, food delivery, streaming and financial platforms.Snapchat, Roblox, Fortnite, Ring, Coinbase, Venmo, Robinhood, Hinge, and Reddit, and others, were among the many services to suffer issues.Amazon said at the time the outage was a result of a domain name system resolution issue—the process where a computer turns a website domain name into an IP address."There’s no sign that this AWS [Amazon Web Services] outage was caused by a cyberattack—it looks like a technical fault affecting one of Amazon’s main data centers," said Rob Jardin, chief digital officer at cybersecurity firm NymVPN, in a statement last year."These issues can happen when systems become overloaded or a key part of the network goes down, and because so many websites and apps rely on AWS, the impact spreads quickly."Update 3/26/2026 5.30 a.m. ET: This article has been updated with more informationIn a polarized era, the center is dismissed as bland.
